# My Plan for This Year

I've been working this land since I was 14. I know what grows here and what doesn't. Quzhou soil is good but dry — my well is what keeps me going. My main income is wheat and maize. The vegetables and stevia are extra cash.

**Wheat and Maize (same 7 mu, rotating):** I'll plant wheat in October like always. I use the improved seeds the seed station sells — the local traditional ones don't yield as much anymore. I'll rotary-till after maize harvest, then apply base fertilizer before seeding. I'll irrigate four times: at sowing, wintering, jointing, and heading if it's dry. Come June I harvest wheat, then immediately plant hybrid maize. For maize I usually skip the plow and just rotary-till — saves time and fuel. Two fertilizer applications: base at planting and topdress at jointing. Three irrigations should be enough.

**Cabbage (1.5 mu, autumn):** I transplant seedlings in August. Cabbage drinks a lot of water and needs potassium for the head. Five irrigations, and I'll spray three times — aphids and caterpillars come every year.

**Cauliflower (1 mu, spring):** Plant early spring. Similar to cabbage but less water needed. Two pesticide sprays usually enough.

**Chili (0.5 mu, spring-summer):** This one needs the most spraying — thrips and spider mites are constant trouble. Six irrigations through the long harvest period. I'll apply fertilizer in splits.

**Eggplant (0.5 mu, spring-summer):** Easy crop for me. Good market nearby. Keep moisture consistent or the fruit cracks.

**Stevia (1.5 mu, spring-summer):** I've grown this three years now. The buyers come to collect. Less fertilizer than vegetables, but I need to cut it twice before frost.
